title: EnvironmentFactor
description: A single named environmental condition of a test run (operating system, network characteristic, locale, hardware configuration or dependency version) pinned to a concrete value or constraint and recorded because it changes how tests behave. It describes one factor of the execution environment, not the test type that bundles factors together nor any input supplied to the system under test. Use ContextVariation instead when the thing being modelled is a named test context (functional, load, security, regression, smoke, exploratory) that groups several environmental constraints, rather than one variable with one value. Use PartitionValue instead when the value is an equivalence class of an input field passed to the system under test (request parameter, form field, data property), not a property of the runtime environment. Use InputSpacePartition instead when an input dimension is being divided into equivalence classes. Do this even if that dimension is a locale or OS selector. A single fixed environmental setting is not a partition.

factorType.description: Category of environmental variable being documented.

value.description: The specific value or constraint for this factor (e.g., 'Ubuntu 22.04', 'latency < 100ms', 'en-US', 'Node.js 20.x').

expectedRange.description: Acceptable range or set of values for this factor in the test environment (e.g., 'latency 50-200ms', 'Ubuntu 20.04 or 22.04').

testImpact.description: Description of how variations in this factor are expected to affect test behavior or outcomes.

description.description: Free-text explanation of what this environmental factor is and why it is pinned for testing, for example 'Server-side timezone forced to UTC to make date-boundary tests deterministic'. Set it whenever the factorType and value alone do not make the factor's purpose clear.

x-dr-standard: IEEE 829-2008 Test Design Specification / Test Plan §'Environmental needs' (hardware, software, communications and tool characteristics of the test environment)
x-dr-evidence: A CI matrix entry pinning an environment axis, such as a GitHub Actions `strategy.matrix` with `os: [ubuntu-22.04, windows-2022]` or `node-version: [18.x, 20.x]`, or a tox/nox env list over Python versions.

Test setup that forces an environmental condition, such as setting `TZ`/`LANG`/`LC_ALL` environment variables, network-throttling or latency-injection config (toxiproxy, tc netem, Playwright `emulateNetworkConditions`), or a docker-compose test service pinned to a specific image tag.

Conditional test guards keyed on the environment, such as `@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == 'win32')`, Jest `testEnvironment`, or an engines/`.nvmrc`/`.tool-versions` file referenced by test configuration.
